note: Criterion-by-criterion reconciliation of the approved Goal's 31 acceptance criteria against committed evidence, plus the computed coverage reconciliation the Goal's criterion 12 asks for. Every verdict is drawn from a closed set of three: MET (direct evidence cited), MET-AS-ADJUDICATED (the criterion as literally written was narrowed or made vacuous by a recorded decision, with the delta stated), NOT-MET (with a stop report naming what would close it). The `coverage` block is COMPUTED from the committed ledger and the six committed wave censuses by scripts/goal-integration-reconciliation-cli.mjs and re-checked on every test run; it is not restated prose. This record proves no visual, geographic, architectural or performance claim of its own - it cites the wave records that measured those. T029 (Issue #62) UPDATE. Four of the six NOT-MET criteria - 7, 8, 24 and 30 - were closed by measurement and, for criterion 8, by a build. Each carries `priorVerdict`, `priorStopReport` and `closedBy` so the original refusal and the stop report that named it stay readable beside the closure; nothing was rewritten to look as though it had always passed. The open set is now exactly the structural pair, criteria 1 and 22, and the ADR's STOP recommendation stands on that pair alone. T007 (Issue #72) AMENDMENT. Criterion 22 is closed as MET-AS-ADJUDICATED on a user decision recorded 2026-08-15, and criterion 1 is deliberately NOT closed with it; the open set is now exactly criterion 1. The closing evidence is the manhattan-citywide-default-streaming goal's own acceptance record, cited in `closures.evidenceRecords` with its checksum and carrying a NOT-MET of its own. Criterion 1's stop report is amended rather than replaced in spirit: gap (a), the retention gap that the 512-entry all-resident cache contract bounded, is structurally closed by the shipped visibility scheduler; what remains is the generated-exterior gap for the 41,357 parents that draw as sourced base massing and the still-unadjudicated 899 grammar refusals. The `coverage` block is untouched by this amendment and still recomputes byte-equal from the committed ledger and censuses.

criteriaDerivation.method: SHA-256 over the 31 criterion strings joined by a single newline, in declared order, with no trailing newline.
criteriaDerivation.note: The Goal ledger lives outside this repository and is deliberately not vendored here, so no test can read it. Re-run the command above against the live ledger to confirm this record judged the criteria the Goal actually declares.

verdicts.stopReport: AMENDED BY T007 (Issue #72). ONE OF THE TWO GAPS IS STRUCTURALLY CLOSED; THE OTHER IS WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS THE SUBSTANTIVE ONE. (a) RETENTION - CLOSED AS A STRUCTURE. This stop report originally said the gap was bounded by the 512-entry all-resident exterior cache contract (EXTERIOR_RUNTIME_BUDGETS.maxCacheEntries), and that ADR 0024 cell scheduling was the named structural prerequisite, so that until it existed 'promote more of a wave' and 'raise the cache cap' were the same decision. That prerequisite now exists and is on by default: visibility-driven cell scheduling ships (ADR 0041), its residency is certified at a 128-cell pool (ADR 0042), and the 512-entry cap is no longer the binder - the measured default session holds 128 resident cells against 883 visible, and the EXTERIOR cell cache it governs sits at 40 entries and 14,369,372 B, 7.8% of its 512-entry ceiling and 5.3% of its 256 MiB ceiling. Stated precisely, because two caches are easy to conflate: the 58,243,420 B over 99 entries measured at that station belongs to the SEPARATE citywide dense shard cache, whose own resolved budget is 112 shards / 83,886,080 B - that is 69.4% of its bytes and 88.4% of its entries, which is pressure rather than headroom. What closed for this criterion is the exterior cache's entry cap, not a claim of headroom everywhere. Breadth is now a function of what the camera can see, exactly as the prerequisite promised. (b) GENERATED EXTERIORS - OPEN, AND UNCHANGED IN KIND. A default session draws 41,841 buildings at the island overview, but 484 of them carry a GENERATED exterior; the other 41,357 draw as sourced base massing - a real footprint extruded to a sourced height, which is real geometry and is not a generated exterior. This criterion asks for a detailed, visually complete generated exterior at the target baseline LODs for every accepted parent, and that is still 484. Closing it requires materializing and retaining generated exteriors for the remaining parents, which is a data-production task and not a runtime one; the scheduler that used to block it no longer does. (c) REFUSALS - OPEN, AND STILL A USER DECISION. The grammar refuses 899 of 45,194 owned parents outright under named stop codes (864 at the plan stage, 35 at the asset stage; dominated by source-height-below-grammar-minimum 384 and ring-vertex-count-unsupported 324). Either extend the grammar to close them, or record a user adjudication that a tombstoned refusal under a named stop code satisfies this criterion. No such adjudication record exists in this repository, and T007 did not create one: the user's 2026-08-15 decision closed criterion 22 only and left criterion 1 open.

LEGIBILITY IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Legs 1 and 4 pass only if the disclosure has area, sits inside the viewport, is NOT clamped to a single line, fits its own box, and survives a nine-point hit test with nothing painted over it. The first re-capture under this instrument FAILED both legs, which is how the defect below was found and fixed rather than described.

THE OCCLUSION DEFECT IS REPAIRED, and it was a stylesheet defect rather than a wiring one. `.runtime-note span` clamps the lane to one ellipsised row and the 680px breakpoint caps the lane at calc(100% - 160px), so a ~300-character sentence could never render whatever the DOM said. src/styles.css now releases the clamp for this line at (0,2,1) specificity, lifts it off the notices lane's z-index, removes the lane's max-height clip for it, and caps its width at calc(100vw - 56px). Measured after the fix: white-space normal, 11px, 7 wrapped lines, textFitsItsBox true, insideViewport true, occludedPoints 0 of 9.

aria-pressed on the render-profile controls now follows the EFFECTIVE profile rather than the requested one. Reporting the requested profile pressed told a screen-reader user that the finest LOD was in force while the coarsest was rendering; the requested-but-not-rendered state is disclosed in the control's title and in data-profile-requested rather than discarded.
verdicts.adjudicationDelta: Three deltas, one of which is a real defect found by looking at the capture rather than at the counters. (a) EMULATED, NOT A DEVICE. Chrome's device metrics override with mobile: true, touch emulation and an iOS user-agent string measures the application's response to a mobile viewport, touch capability and user agent. It says nothing about a real phone's GPU, memory ceiling, thermal behaviour, browser engine or network, and no such claim is made. (b) SELECTION IS DEEP-LINK-DRIVEN, NOT A TOUCH PICK. A tap dispatched at a guessed canvas pixel would not identify WHICH feature was picked, so the leg claims deep-link selection and details; native Cesium picking is evidenced on the desktop class by criterion 10. (c) THE TRUTHFUL FALLBACK NOTICE STILL OCCLUDES THE MAP. The 'Exterior streaming fallback' notice - the tombstone statement for the 870 of 883 cells shipping no exterior geometry - is large on a 390px viewport and covers much of the scene in every leg's still. It is honest, it is not cropped out, and it is named per leg in the record's visualState. The lower-LOD disclosure itself is no longer occluded: that defect was found by this task's own legibility instrument, fixed in the stylesheet, and re-captured.

verdicts.criterion: Final Manhattan coverage reconciliation reports zero missing spatial cells, zero missing accepted building parents, zero duplicate canonical owners, and zero unclassified exterior components
evidence: Computed in this record's coverage block by scripts/goal-integration-reconciliation-cli.mjs from the committed ledger and the six committed censuses, and re-checked on every test run by scripts/goal-integration-reconciliation.test.mjs.
missingSpatialCells 0 (883 declared, 883 assigned to a wave, wave cell sum 883).
missingAcceptedBuildingParents 0 (45,194 declared, 45,194 distinct ids across the 883 cells).
duplicateCanonicalOwners 0 (no building id appears in more than one cell).
buildingsWithoutStyleClass 0 (every wave's style-class distribution sums exactly to its materialized count) and ownedBuildingsAccountedByNeither 0 (owned = materialized + refused in every wave).
stopCodesOutsideClosedVocabulary 0 (all six observed codes are members of MIDTOWN_CORE_V3_STOP_CODES).

SCOPE OF THE COMPONENT HALF. The computed metric is named buildingsWithoutStyleClass because that is what a census can count: buildings missing a machine-readable class. The criterion's 'zero unclassified exterior COMPONENTS' half is carried by criterion 15's contract rather than by a count - a component outside the closed generated / evidence-backed / absent / not-applicable vocabulary makes v3TruthTiers() THROW, so an unclassified component cannot reach a release for a census to find. The zero is enforced upstream, not measured downstream.

WHAT THIS CRITERION READS, so that MET here does not contradict NOT-MET at criterion 1. This is a LEDGER-PARTITION reading: every declared cell belongs to exactly one wave and every accepted parent is owned exactly once, which is a statement about the immutable ownership partition and says nothing about whether a parent's exterior was ever built or shipped. Criterion 1 asks the MISSING-EXTERIOR question over the same 45,194 parents and answers 484 shipped, 899 refused. Both are true simultaneously because they count different things: ownership closure versus exterior presence.

verdicts.adjudicationDelta: THE ENVELOPE REACHES A TIER, AND THE TIER IS NOT THE ONE A 2026-08-12 READER OF THIS RECORD WOULD HAVE PICTURED. When this criterion was graded NOT-MET, 'the user-approved exterior tier' was read as a generated exterior for every accepted parent, and the gap was stated as 484 of 45,194. What the default session now delivers is a TWO-TIER composition: sourced base massing island-wide - real footprints extruded to sourced heights, with per-building pick identity - plus textured V3 exteriors within the near-camera radius. So the count that closes this criterion (41,841 drawn) and the count that does not close criterion 1 (484 with a generated exterior) are counts of DIFFERENT THINGS, and collapsing them would be the overstatement this record exists to refuse. The adjudication is that the user-approved contract for the closing goal defines that two-tier composition AS the tier the envelope was to reach, and the envelope reaches it without a stable-id, selection, deep-link, provenance or failure-state regression. It is graded MET-AS-ADJUDICATED and not MET because the criterion's own words are ambiguous between the two readings, and the reading that closes it is the one the user approved rather than the one this record originally applied. Criterion 1 is deliberately NOT closed by the same decision: see its stop report.

That caveat is why the reading was superseded rather than treated as a defect, and it is also why the superseding readings had to force collection to say anything at all.

The SUPERSEDING readings, both with forced collection: Block 835 V3 (T026) heap SHRANK 13.3% and 12.0%, and Midtown -0.107 and -0.105 against a 0.10 band. Both are prose over untracked raw files rather than committed records, and both predate the four textured waves.

RETAINED MEMORY IS NOT CERTIFIED FOR WHAT SHIPS. grep -rn 'monoton' over data/ returns zero hits: no committed record for any of the six waves carries a first-half/second-half growth ratio, a noise-band comparison, or a pass/fail. The 12 heapAfterGcBytes readings in each acceptance record are 3 repeats across 4 DIFFERENT camera stations, not repeats of one deterministic camera path. The only monotonic-growth verdicts are the two superseding readings named above, and nothing covers the four textured waves or the six-wave composition.

Also unmeasured: there is no committed peak-concurrency measurement for the six-wave composition (grep -rn 'peakConcurren' over data/ returns zero); the four acceptance records carry maxConcurrentRequests as a CONFIGURATION value, not a measured peak.

T029 CLOSURE of the retained-memory conjunct, measured where it had never been measured. data/goal-bounded-gaps-20260812/heap-concurrency-evidence.json (sha256 625a8d62fe0a78405a03923f2a80c4da788a5b6d1943243cb4237116d65bfa12): the existing block835CanaryHeapVerdict method - first-half versus second-half MEDIAN against a 0.1 noise band - over 4 REPEATS of the committed deterministic 8-pose path on the SIX-WAVE DEFAULT composition, with forcedCollection TRUE (window.gc via --js-flags=--expose-gc) before every sample. growthRatio -0.134: the heap SHRANK. monotonicGrowthDetected FALSE.

TWO runs are reported rather than only the committed one, and they are NOT equally evidenced. The COMMITTED, CHECKSUMMED run is the one cited above: growthRatio -0.134. An EARLIER run of the same subcommand, taken before the residency disclosure was added to the CLI, read growthRatio +0.0228; its record was OVERWRITTEN by the re-run and there is no checksummed artifact for it, so it is reported here as an uncommitted prior reading and nothing rests on it. Both returned monotonicGrowthDetected false, which is why it is worth stating that the verdict did not depend on a single sample of a noisy quantity - but only the -0.134 reading is auditable.

THE MEASURED PEAK CONCURRENCY, which grep -rn 'peakConcurren' data/ previously returned zero hits for: 4, read from the aggregate request budget's own peak counter across the whole session including the cold load - not the configured maxConcurrentRequests the four wave acceptance records carry. Cache in the same session, restated from the cited record rather than from a console line: peak 1,910,784 bytes against the 256 MiB budget, cachePass true, zero external hosts. verdicts.adjudicationDelta: Two narrowings, both recorded in the evidence record itself rather than only here. (a) THE RESIDENT WORKING SET IS SMALL, AND VARIABLE. All six waves are ACTIVE - this is the promoted default composition - but the committed camera path stays inside one midtown block, so the resident exterior cache held 14 entries in every one of the four repeats of the committed run - and 109 in the uncommitted earlier one - against a 512-entry ceiling, with ZERO evictions throughout. This record therefore certifies retention ACROSS REPEATS OF A DETERMINISTIC PATH, which is the criterion's own wording, and does NOT certify behaviour at peak residency or under eviction pressure. (b) THE MEASUREMENT REQUIRED A PROBE-HARNESS BUILD. The in-app canary probe is compiled out of an ordinary production bundle, so this ran against a build differing from production by the VITE_BLOCK835_PROBE flag alone; the probe observes the runtime and changes no pin, no eligibility and no load path, and the served-bundle gate records the exact bytes measured. The reading remains JS-heap-only: native GPU and decoded-texture retention are not observable from this instrument, as the method's own bounded claim states.

The acceptance CLIs already force collection and read usedJSHeapSize; only the repeated-single-path shape and the growth verdict are missing. A second, smaller item: record the measured peak concurrent exterior request count for the six-wave session alongside it.

residualRisks: THE VOLUME-MARGIN PATTERN IS STILL UNEXPLAINED. The wave-scale worst accepted volume-identity deviation sat at 0.988 of tolerance for central-upper-Manhattan and 0.9895 for northern-Manhattan, and the latter refused 16 buildings for exceeding it. Two waves in a row above ninety-eight hundredths of the tolerance is a pattern, not a coincidence. No tolerance was moved and no task has explained it; ADR 0037 precondition (e) records that the explanation is still owed.

LOAD-DEPENDENT TEST FLAKES. src/release/midtown-core-v3-release.test.ts and src/app/App.test.tsx time out under concurrent CPU load (vitest's 5,000 ms default) and pass in isolation and on an unloaded machine. midtown-core-v3-release.test.ts alone takes about 20 s for 20 tests. These are timeouts, not assertion failures. The isolating measurement: `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` passed 1,535 of 1,535 twice in a row at about 72 s, while the default parallel run intermittently drops exactly one of these two files. So the trigger is worker CPU contention, not test order or shared state, and `--no-file-parallelism` is a reliable workaround for a loaded machine. A raised `testTimeout` would close it properly.

REPAIRED IN T029 - THE T023 SMOKE JOURNEY IS NOW REPRODUCIBLE FROM A CLEAN BROWSER PROFILE. The finding stands as recorded: a fresh Chrome profile issues /favicon.ico, the showcase allowlist classifier had no category for it, and everyRequestClassified read false (554 distinct URLs against the committed record's 553). The repair adds a CLASSIFICATION, not an exemption: PUBLIC_SHOWCASE_BROWSER_IMPLICIT_PATHS is a closed, exact-match set, a browser-implicit request is reported in the record with the answer it received, and the journey additionally requires that none of them was answered with a payload - the observed /favicon.ico returned 404. Re-run fresh on 2026-08-12 from a NEW profile: 554 observed, 554 classified, all three journeys passed. The classifier still refuses a planted foreign path, which is asserted by a test.

REPAIRED IN T029 - THE SHOWCASE DIFFERENTIAL AUDIT NO LONGER DEPENDS ON WHICH EVIDENCE DIRECTORIES EXIST. The finding stands as recorded: workingRecordDirectories counted whatever sat under data/, so T024 creating its own record directory moved the count from 19 to 20 and changed the record's checksum. The repair is exclude-by-declared-set: scripts/public-showcase-audit-cli.mjs declares AUDITED_WORKING_RECORD_DIRECTORIES and intersects the scan with it, so a directory committed by a later task cannot move these bytes, while a DECLARED directory that is absent or empty fails the audit rather than shrinking the count. Verified empirically: a planted sibling record directory left the re-emitted record byte-identical (sha256 d9c4ec94f87cdcd7e533ae4fa0241f140d7fa01322dac58e5df6ed255f0346ca before and after). Widening the scope is now a deliberate, reviewable edit to a constant.

THE WAVE LEDGER'S eligibility.json IS IMMUTABLE AND NOW READS STALE. It declares all 883 cells private-eligible and 0 public-eligible, with a basis stating no cell is public-eligible until a promotion task supplies per-cell rights-cleared evidence. Six promotions have since shipped public roots under per-wave instruments. The artifact is v1, pinned to the ledger checksum, and correctly was not mutated; the live eligibility authority is the six approval instruments, not this file.

STRUCTURAL VALIDATION IS NOT VISUAL, GEOGRAPHIC OR PRODUCTION PROOF. A signed-volume identity, a checksum and a passing suite do not prove that a facade looks right, that a building sits where the real one does, or that the composition is smooth. The near-field visual reading is Block-835-scoped, and the isolated slow frames of 116.2 ms and 140.0 ms are recorded rather than smoothed.

THE PRIVACY AND EVIDENCE MACHINERY HAS ONLY EVER RUN ON SYNTHETIC FIXTURES. No self-captured evidence exists in the repository, no committed record carries a redactedArtifactRef, and ADR 0022 records that the privacy review is attestation-only and that a missed face or plate is not detected.

THE FOUR T029 CLOSURES ARE ADJUDICATED, NOT CLEAN. The 1440p capture inherits the deep-link camera-height clamp and its composition reading is a human reading of 3 of 16 stills; the mobile journey is emulated and its selection leg is deep-link-driven rather than a touch pick; the keyboard traversal runs on DevTools-emulated focus rather than OS focus; and the heap verdict covers a camera path whose resident working set was 14 entries of a 512-entry ceiling with zero evictions in the committed run, so nothing is certified at peak residency or under eviction pressure. Each delta is stated on its own criterion.

REPAIRED IN T029 - THE MOBILE LOWER-LOD DISCLOSURE IS NOW LEGIBLE AT 390 CSS PX. The finding stands as recorded: the disclosure was in the DOM with role=status and structurally unreadable, clamped to one ellipsised row by `.runtime-note span` inside a calc(100% - 160px) lane. It was a stylesheet defect. The repair releases the clamp for this line only, lifts it above the notices lane, removes the lane's max-height clip for it and caps its width to the viewport; measured after the fix, it renders on 7 wrapped lines at 11px, fits its box, sits inside the viewport and survives a nine-point hit test unoccluded. The mobile journey now measures legibility rather than DOM presence, and FAILED both affected legs before the fix. What remains is the large truthful fallback notice, which is named per leg.

amendments.decision: USER DECISION, recorded 2026-08-15: close criterion 22 only. Criterion 1 remains NOT-MET.
amendments.statement: One criterion closed, one deliberately left open, by a decision that was the user's to make rather than an implementer's. Criterion 22 asks whether the approved coverage envelope reaches its user-approved exterior tier without regressions, and the tier is now defined by a user-approved Goal contract that the shipped default session satisfies and that this record cites by digest. Criterion 1 asks for a generated exterior for every accepted parent, and 41,357 of the 41,841 buildings a default session draws are sourced base massing rather than generated exteriors - so closing 22 does not close 1, and grading them together would have turned a structural change into a claim about data that was never produced. The T029 discipline is kept: criterion 22 carries priorVerdict, priorStopReport and closedBy, so the original refusal and the stop report that named it stay readable beside the closure. Criterion 1's stop report was UPDATED IN PLACE rather than duplicated, because the record's own shape rule forbids a priorStopReport on a criterion that is still NOT-MET; the amended text therefore states what the original said and which half of it closed.
